notes.interpretation: Training had clear measurable effect — composite score moved -0.39 from a baseline of 0.54. Unlike the GSM8K runs (gradient effectively zero), this shows GSPO is actively updating the policy on the bundled support corpus. The direction is wrong: most likely overfitting — 3 epochs over 16 training scenarios x group_size=4 = ~192 rollouts on a rule-based rubric (keyword acknowledgement, length-window politeness check, safety multiplier) is enough to push LoRA r=16 into a degenerate optimum that no longer matches the keyword-based grading. The baseline of 0.54 already shows Qwen3.5-0.8B handles a substantial fraction of these rubric items zero-shot.
remaining_hypotheses: Overfitting on tiny corpus (most likely): drop num_epochs 3 -> 1, or expand the bundled corpus past 24 total scenarios.
GSPO clip range 3e-4/4e-4 at this rollout count produces sharp updates that overshoot for keyword-based rewards (which have discrete cliffs in the score landscape — present/absent terms).
Reward function is keyword-brittle; a paraphrase-tolerant LLM-judge reward (also shipped) might score the trained model's actual quality differently.
8 eval scenarios = 12.5% resolution per example -> high variance; even -0.39 needs multiple seeds to confirm direction.
notes.framework_evidence: This is the first run in the session where the policy actually moved — proving the gradient path (GSPO clipped surrogate -> LoRA backward) works end-to-end. The two GSM8K runs both showed pass@1 0.0 -> 0.0; this run shows 0.54 -> 0.15. Wrong direction, but the training loop is functional.
notes.v1_publication_gates: FAIL — improvement is negative; requires positive improvement with three seeds in agreement per benchmark_results/SCHEMA.md.
